headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Devin can write shared integrations while Prefect can egress broadly, creating default-path data leakage and action-cascade risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browsers, files, and shared integrations; Prefect exposes API-based orchestration surfaces. A shared filesystem or integration channel could let attacker-controlled content flow from Devin into Prefect-like automation, but the exact bridge is not documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Devin writes untrusted content into a shared repo, Slack thread, or MCP-backed artifact
IF Prefect consumes that artifact as workflow input without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict shared channels to read-only for one side
Add provenance tags to all handoff artifacts
Require manual approval before Prefect consumes Devin outputs
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitizing adapters

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and handles secrets in a cloud workspace with broad egress. Prefect has broad network egress and workflow metadata handling. If they share any workspace or integration, sensitive material can leave the boundary by default; the blast radius includes code and secrets, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Devin and Prefect share a workspace, repo, or OAuth principal
IF Devin processes secrets or private code while Prefect can observe or transmit workflow metadata
mitigations: Separate credentials and OAuth principals
Disable shared workspace mounts
Limit Devin to non-sensitive repos
Audit outbound destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: add DLP and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run in parallel sessions; Prefect orchestrates pipelines and can call GitHub APIs. Overlapping writes to shared repos or workflow state can race even without explicit locks. The profiles do not prove a shared mutable target, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository, branch, or workflow metadata store
IF no external locking or merge gate is enabled
mitigations: Assign separate branches or queues
Enable branch protection and merge checks
Serialize writes with a lock file or lease
Make one agent read-only on shared resources
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can produce code, docs, and operational artifacts; Prefect is an orchestration system that can act on workflow metadata and APIs. If Prefect treats Devin output as authoritative, errors can cascade into automated downstream actions. Because the pair’s interaction is undocumented, uncertainty favors high.
conditions: IF Prefect ingests Devin-generated artifacts without verification
IF those artifacts trigger pipeline execution, deployment, or notifications
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Validate Devin outputs against schemas
Add checksum or signature verification
Route Devin output through a staging queue
requires-engineering: enforce policy gates in Prefect

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and integration tokens in a vendor-managed cloud workspace, while Prefect is documented only as workflow metadata tooling. If EU PII or regulated data enters Devin’s cloud integrations and then flows through Prefect, retention or residency mismatches are plausible. The profiles do not prove a specific regime, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is processed in Devin’s integrations
IF Prefect stores or logs the same records under a different retention or residency policy
mitigations: Classify data before routing it
Keep regulated data out of shared workflows
Review retention settings on both systems
Document residency for each integration
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing
